sentences.text: Choyrodon barsboldi is the sole known species within its genus and belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea. It is classified as a basal member of Iguanodontia, a group of ornithopod dinosaurs.

The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, includes a partial skeleton with a skull, lower jaws, cervical ribs, and metacarpals. The skull possesses a supraoccipital bone that overlaps on both sides, a structure researchers interpret as an opisthotic bone.
The genus name combines the Mongolian city of Choyr with the Latin word for tooth, while the species name honors paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.
American paleontologist Terry Gates and colleagues formally named this dinosaur in 2018.

Three distinct specimens of Choyrodon have been found in the lower member of the Khuren Dukh Formation. The holotype specimen MPC-D 100/801 was discovered in the lower deposits of the Choeren Doe formation dating to the middle Albian.

Phylogenetic analysis identifies Choyrodon as the sister taxon of Eolambia. Choyrodon is distinguished from the coexisting Altirhinus by the presence of an open antorbital fenestra, a feature absent in the holotype of Altirhinus.

Choyrodon lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) in the Khuren Dukh Formation of Mongolia. It lived approximately 110 to 100 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia. The fossil record for Choyrodon spans from 110.1 to 100.5 million years ago.

While some suggest Choyrodon is merely a juvenile Altirhinus, the describers argue against this based on specific anatomical differences. Researchers found no evidence to support the hypothesis that Choyrodon is a juvenile form of Altirhinus.
